title: Falafel
subtitle: Crisp chickpea fritters
excerpt: Spiced chickpea fritters made from soaked raw chickpeas ground with herbs and aromatics, then fried until golden and crisp. The outside is crunchy, the inside is bright green and tender.

recipe.sourceNotes: Falafel is a staple street food across the Levant and Egypt. The Egyptian version (ta'amiya) is made with broad beans; the Levantine version uses chickpeas. Both are ancient in origin. The dish is now widespread across the Middle East and has become popular globally.

recipeTools.notes: Essential for grinding the chickpeas to the right texture.
Or a deep saucepan with a thermometer.

content.text: Falafel are fried chickpea fritters with a crisp, golden exterior and a bright green, herby interior. The key is to use dried chickpeas that have been soaked overnight, never tinned. Tinned chickpeas are too wet and will fall apart in the oil. The overnight soak is not negotiable.

items.preparation: soaked overnight in cold water and drained

content.text: Drain the soaked chickpeas well and pat dry on a clean tea towel. Place in a food processor with the onion, garlic, parsley, coriander, cumin, ground coriander, salt, and pepper. Pulse to a coarse paste, scraping down the sides as needed. It should hold together when pressed but not be completely smooth.
Add the baking powder and sesame seeds and pulse once or twice to combine. Transfer to a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oil to 180 C. Shape the mixture into balls or small flat patties, about 3 cm across. Fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning halfway, until deep golden brown all over. The inside should read at least 75 C.
Drain on a wire rack. Serve immediately with flatbreads, tahini sauce, and pickled vegetables.
Falafel falling apart in the oil: the mixture is too wet or too coarsely ground. Return to the processor and pulse more, then refrigerate for another 30 minutes before frying.
Pale outside and dry inside: oil is too cool. Wait until it reaches 180 C before adding the next batch.
